skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Use inference.sh CLI examples to generate AI videos with text-to-video, image-to-video, lipsync, avatar, upscaling, foley, and merge workflows.
skill.summary: Generate AI video workflows through inference.sh CLI examples for 40+ models.
skill.author: toolshell

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are Markdown backtick false positives around tables and code fences. Real risk remains because the skill intentionally runs inference.sh CLI commands, may send prompts or media URLs to remote video providers, embeds one remote image, and gives shell examples without escaping guidance.

remediation.issue: External CLI and remote model execution are central to the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy notice that prompts, image URLs, audio URLs, and video URLs may be sent to inference.sh or model providers.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use single-quoted JSON inputs that users may modify.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to JSON-encode and shell-escape user-provided prompts and URLs before running infsh commands.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends npx commands for related skill installation.
remediation.suggestion: Limit related installation commands or add verification guidance for source, ref, and permissions before installing extra skills.

remediation.issue: A remote Markdown image is embedded from cloud.inference.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Use a local marketplace asset or document that rendering the README can request remote content.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped User Input Risk in Shell Examples
semantic_findings.description: The examples pass JSON to --input inside shell single quotes. If an agent substitutes raw user prompts or URLs without escaping, quote characters in user content can alter shell parsing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file contains static examples rather than vulnerable executable code. The skill is intended to adapt user media prompts into these Bash commands, and no escaping guidance is provided.

content.value_statement: Video teams need quick access to many AI video models. This skill provides CLI examples for text-to-video, image animation, lipsync, upscaling, foley, and merging.
actual_capabilities: Lists inference.sh app IDs for Google Veo, Grok, Seedance, Wan, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, and utility models.
Shows text-to-video examples with prompt and duration inputs for supported models.
Shows image-to-video examples that animate a supplied image URL.
Shows avatar and lipsync workflows that combine image and audio URLs.
Includes examples for video upscaling, foley sound generation, and clip merging.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps and streaming results.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a working account session.
Runs external CLI commands and sends prompts or media URLs to remote services.
Does not include validation or escaping helpers for user-provided prompt text.
Output quality, generation time, and cost depend on the selected model provider.

use_cases.title: Draft Social Media Video Concepts
use_cases.description: Create short text-to-video prompts and select a fast model for campaign tests.

use_cases.title: Animate Product or Storyboard Images
use_cases.description: Turn a reference image URL into an image-to-video request with a matching model.

use_cases.title: Prototype Media Pipelines
use_cases.description: Combine generation, lipsync, upscaling, foley, and merging commands into a repeatable workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Short Product Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a five-second product video for [product]. Recommend a suitable inference.sh video model and the input fields I should provide.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Reference Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this image URL for [scene goal]. Choose an image-to-video model and describe the motion prompt, aspect ratio, and duration.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Avatar Narration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking-head workflow using this portrait URL and narration audio URL. Select a lipsync model and list required safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Step Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a video pipeline for [campaign]. Include model selection, generation, upscaling, foley sound, clip merging, review steps, and privacy checks.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a nature timelapse video.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a Veo text-to-video model, refines the visual prompt, and identifies the duration setting for the CLI run.

output_examples.input: A user wants a portrait to speak with recorded narration.
output_examples.output: The skill selects an avatar or lipsync model, requests image and audio URLs, and warns that both assets go to a remote provider.

output_examples.input: A user has two generated clips that need polish.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests upscaling, optional foley sound, and a merge step with a simple transition plan.

best_practices: Review the selected model, provider, cost, and data handling terms before running a command.
Escape or encode user-provided prompts and URLs before inserting them into shell commands.
Use non-sensitive media unless the provider terms allow the content and your organization approves it.
anti_patterns: Running generated commands without checking the model ID and destination service.
Sending private faces, voices, customer footage, or unreleased assets without approval.
Treating placeholder URLs from examples as production-ready media sources.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos directly?
faq.answer: It provides inference.sh CLI workflows. Actual generation happens through the external CLI and selected model provider.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The generated report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The quick start requires the inference.sh CLI and login before running model commands.

faq.question: Can it animate existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video examples using Wan and Seedance models with image URL inputs.

faq.question: Can it create talking-head videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse examples for avatar and lipsync workflows.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm provider terms, avoid sensitive media, review generated commands, and escape user-provided text.
